artworks.title: The Flaying of Marsyas
artworks.description: Titian's Kroměříž masterpiece — Apollo's assistants flay the defeated satyr hung upside down, pain and music dissolving in late paint.

artworks.title: Apollo Flaying Marsyas
artworks.description: Ribera's Brussels canvas — luminous Apollo peels the skin from Marsyas in a shaft of light, the contest's aftermath as Spanish tenebrism.

artworks.title: Athena and Marsyas
artworks.year: Roman copy after a Greek bronze of c. 450 BC
artworks.description: After Myron: Athena has discarded the aulos; Marsyas starts forward to claim the pipes — the step before hubris and Apollo's knife.

artworks.title: The Flaying of Marsyas
artworks.description: Bronzino's Hermitage panel stages the musical contest itself — Florentine Mannerism before the flaying.

artworks.title: Apollo and Marsyas
artworks.description: Perugino's Louvre panel — lyre against pipes in Umbrian calm, the deadly rivalry still a quiet pastoral exchange.

popCulture.title: Marsyas
popCulture.description: The aulos contest and the flaying remain Western art's rawest music lesson — challenge Apollo, lose your skin.
